entities.summary: Jeongjong of Joseon, personal name Yi Bang-gwa, later Yi Gyeong, was the second monarch of the Joseon dynasty of Korea. Born around 1390, he ascended to the throne in 1400 after the death of his half-brother, King Taejong. Jeongjong's reign was marked by a series of military campaigns against the Mongols and the Yuan dynasty of China, which had established a strategic foothold in Korea. His military successes helped to secure Joseon's borders and expand its influence in the region. Despite his military achievements, Jeongjong's reign was also marked by internal conflicts and power struggles, which ultimately led to his downfall. He died in 1419 and was succeeded by his son, King Sejong. Jeongjong's legacy as a military leader and statesman has endured, and he remains one of the most important figures in Korean history. His policies and military campaigns had a lasting impact on the development of Joseon and its relationships with neighboring countries. The Joseon dynasty, which Jeongjong helped to establish, went on to become one of the most prosperous and influential empires in Korean history. The legacy of Jeongjong's military campaigns and diplomatic efforts continues to shape Korea's foreign policy and national identity to this day.
